learn.hook: A butterfly's wings, a temple gate, a diya. What is special about their two sides?
points: Some things look the same on both sides of a middle line. We call them symmetrical.
A butterfly, a leaf, a kite and the front of a temple often have matching sides.
At a fair, you see repeating patterns on pots, carpets, bangles and floor tiles.
A pattern repeats a part again and again. Symmetry means one half matches the other half.

example.q: Is a kite with the same design on both sides of its middle stick symmetrical?

learn.reallife: Fair stalls are full of symmetry: pottery, block-printed cloth and painted masks.

games.title: Patterns and symmetry
items: A symmetrical thing has two matching halves.
A repeating pattern always has a part that comes again and again.
Many objects are not, like the letter F.
Floor tiles at a fair often make patterns.

quiz.q: Which is symmetrical?
quiz.explain: A butterfly's wings match on both sides.
steps: Symmetrical means one half matches the other half.
A torn paper, the letter F and a scribble have halves that do not match.
A butterfly's wings match on both sides.

quiz.q: What does symmetrical mean?
options: One half matches the other half
quiz.explain: Both halves are the same, like mirror images.
steps: One half matches the other half, like a mirror image.
It is not about size or colour.
Answer: One half matches the other half
quiz.mistake: Thinks it is about size or colour

quiz.q: A bangle stall has bangles in the pattern red, gold, red, gold... What kind of pattern is it?
quiz.explain: Red, gold repeats again and again.
steps: Red, gold comes again and again.
A part that comes again and again makes a repeating pattern.

quiz.q: Which is NOT symmetrical?
quiz.explain: G does not match if folded.
steps: A kite, a leaf and a diya have matching sides.
The letter G does not match when folded.

quiz.q: Tiles on a fair path go: square, triangle, square, triangle. What comes next?
quiz.explain: The pattern repeats square, triangle.

quiz.q: A symmetrical shape is folded on its line of symmetry. How many matching halves do you get?
quiz.explain: Two halves that match.
steps: Folding on the line of symmetry makes two halves.

quiz.q: Which fair item is often symmetrical?
quiz.explain: Masks are made with matching left and right sides.
steps: Torn, messy and broken things do not have matching sides.
A painted mask is made with matching left and right sides.

quiz.q: A carpet has the pattern ⭐🔷⭐🔷⭐🔷. How many stars are there?
quiz.explain: ⭐ appears 3 times.

teach.ask: Gappu thinks only round things can be symmetrical. Is he right?
teach.praise: No! A butterfly and a kite have matching halves too! Chirp!

revise.summary: Things that look the same on both sides of a middle line are symmetrical. A repeating pattern repeats a part again and again.
focus: Spot symmetrical objects.
Tell symmetry from a repeating pattern.
Continue repeating patterns.
remember: Symmetrical: one half matches the other half.
Butterfly, leaf, kite and temple front often have matching sides.
Red, gold, red, gold is a repeating pattern.
traps: Symmetry is not about size or colour.
Don't just repeat the last item in a pattern.
Count only the shape asked for.

learn.hook: Red, blue, yellow, blue, red. Read it from both ends. Same! That mala is symmetrical.
points: Make malas (strings of beads) using two colours.
A mala in a straight line is symmetrical if it reads the same from both ends.
Red, blue, red is symmetrical. Red, red, blue is not.
With 3 red and 2 blue beads in a row of 5, the middle bead must be red. There are 2 symmetrical ways: R B R B R and B R R R B.
Check by folding the line in the middle: the beads opposite each other must match.

example.q: Is the mala B R B B R B symmetrical?
steps: From the left: B R B B R B
From the right: B R B B R B

learn.reallife: Women at the Surajkund fair make beautiful bead jewellery with matching sides.

games.title: Mala facts
items: A symmetrical mala reads the same from both ends.
R B B R is symmetrical.
With 3 red and 2 blue in a row of 5, the middle can be blue.
Then the 3 reds cannot be paired; the middle must be red.
Folding in the middle checks a mala.

quiz.q: Which mala is symmetrical?
quiz.explain: R B R reads the same from both ends.
steps: A symmetrical mala reads the same from both ends.
R B B → B B R. B R R → R R B. R R B → B R R. Not the same.
R B R → R B R. Same.
quiz.mistake: Picks one that starts and ends differently

quiz.q: Which mala is NOT symmetrical?
quiz.explain: R R B B read backwards is B B R R.
steps: R R R R, B R R B and R B B R read the same.
R R B B backwards is B B R R. Not the same.

quiz.q: A mala has 5 beads: R B ? B R. What colour must the middle be?
quiz.explain: The middle bead has no partner, so any colour keeps it symmetrical.
steps: R B ? B R: the ends match (R, R) and the next match (B, B).
The middle bead is on the fold line. It has no partner.
So any colour keeps it symmetrical.
quiz.mistake: Thinks it must match the ends

quiz.q: With 3 red and 2 blue beads in a row, how many symmetrical malas can be made?
quiz.explain: R B R B R and B R R R B.

quiz.q: A mala starts R B Y. To make it symmetrical with 6 beads, what are the last three?
quiz.explain: The second half mirrors the first: R B Y Y B R.
steps: The second half must mirror the first half.
First half: R B Y. Mirror: Y B R.
Full mala: R B Y Y B R.

quiz.q: How many beads are there in R B R B R?
quiz.explain: Count them: 5 beads.
steps: Count the beads in R B R B R.

quiz.q: In the symmetrical mala B R R R B, how many red beads?
quiz.explain: There are 3 Rs.
steps: Mala: B R R R B.

quiz.q: Is R R B R R symmetrical?
options: Only if the middle is red
quiz.explain: Read backwards it is R R B R R.
steps: Read R R B R R backwards: R R B R R.
It is the same from both ends.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the middle must match the ends

teach.ask: Gappu made a mala: red, yellow, yellow, red. Is it symmetrical, and how can he check?
teach.praise: It reads the same from both ends. It is symmetrical! Chirp!
teach.nudge: What happens when I read it from the other end?

revise.summary: A mala in a line is symmetrical if it reads the same from both ends. The middle bead of an odd mala has no partner.
focus: Check if a mala is symmetrical.
Complete a mala by mirroring.
Find symmetrical ways with given beads.
remember: R B R is symmetrical. R R B is not.
3 red and 2 blue in a row of 5: R B R B R and B R R R B.
Mirror R B Y → R B Y Y B R.
traps: Don't check only one end.
Mirror the beads. Don't just repeat them.
The middle bead does not need to match the ends.

learn.hook: Trace a rangoli, fold it in half. Do the halves match? Then it is symmetrical!
points: Trace a design on thin paper and fold it. If the two halves match exactly, it is symmetrical.
The fold line that splits a design into two matching halves is the line of symmetry.
To complete a half-drawn rangoli, copy each dot and line on the other side, at the same distance from the fold line.
Draw your own symmetrical rangoli on a dot grid: draw one half, then mirror it.
Look around: windows, doors, flowers and leaves are often symmetrical.

example.q: A half-rangoli has a dot 2 squares to the left of the fold line. Where does its partner go?
steps: Same distance on the other side
example.answer: 2 squares to the right of the fold

learn.reallife: Kolams in Tamil Nadu and rangolis in many states are drawn at doorsteps, often with matching halves.

games.title: Rangoli symmetry
items: A matching dot is the same distance from the fold line.
Folding a tracing checks for symmetry.
A line of symmetry can split a design into unequal parts.
A flower with 4 equal petals has symmetry.

games.title: Mirror the dot (fold line in the middle)

items.q: 5 dots on the left half: right half?
4 lines in one half: total in both

quiz.q: How can you check if a rangoli is symmetrical?
options: Trace it, fold it, and see if the halves match
quiz.explain: Matching halves on folding show symmetry.
steps: Trace the rangoli and fold it.
If the two halves match exactly, it is symmetrical.
Colours and weight do not decide it.
Answer: Trace it, fold it, and see if the halves match

quiz.q: What is the line that splits a design into two matching halves called?
quiz.explain: That fold line is the line of symmetry.
steps: The fold line splits a design into two matching halves.
This line is the line of symmetry.

quiz.q: A dot is 3 squares to the right of the fold. Where is its partner?
quiz.explain: Same distance on the other side.
steps: A mirrored dot is at the same distance on the other side.
The dot is 3 squares to the right.
So its partner is 3 squares to the left.

quiz.q: One half of a kolam has 6 dots. How many dots in the full symmetrical kolam (none on the fold)?
steps: One half has 6 dots. None are on the fold.
The other half has 6 matching dots.

quiz.q: Which is a good way to draw your own symmetrical rangoli?
options: Draw one half, then copy it mirrored
quiz.explain: Mirroring one half makes the halves match.
steps: Then copy it mirrored on the other side.
This makes the two halves match.
Answer: Draw one half, then copy it mirrored

quiz.q: Which thing around you is usually symmetrical?
quiz.explain: Windows usually have matching halves.
steps: Spilled, crumpled and broken things are not symmetrical.
A window usually has matching halves.

quiz.q: A half-rangoli shows a petal touching the fold line. In the full design, the petal…
options: Is mirrored on the other side
quiz.explain: Everything is mirrored across the fold.
steps: In a symmetrical design, everything is mirrored across the fold.
So the petal appears again on the other side.
Answer: Is mirrored on the other side

quiz.q: A rangoli has 4 lines of symmetry. Riya found 3. How many more should she look for?
steps: The rangoli has 4 lines. Riya found 3.

teach.ask: Gappu drew half a rangoli. How can he finish it so it is symmetrical?
teach.praise: Copy every dot and line on the other side, the same distance from the fold! Chirp!
teach.nudge: How far from the fold should each copied dot be?

revise.summary: Trace and fold a rangoli to check symmetry. The fold line is the line of symmetry. Copy each dot at the same distance on the other side.
focus: Check symmetry by folding.
Complete a half-drawn rangoli.
Draw your own symmetrical design.
remember: A dot 2 squares left of the fold → partner 2 squares right.
Half has 6 dots (none on the fold) → full has 12.
Windows, doors, flowers and leaves are often symmetrical.
traps: Colours do not decide symmetry.
Don't double the distance. Keep it the same.
Count both halves, not one.

learn.hook: Raise your right hand in front of a mirror. Which hand does your mirror friend raise?
points: A shape is symmetrical if its two halves match exactly when folded.
A mirror image looks the same but with left and right swapped.
If you raise your right hand, your mirror image seems to raise its left hand.
Place a mirror on the middle line of a half-picture. If the reflection completes it, the shape is symmetrical.

example.q: A mask has an eye 3 cm left of the middle. Where should the other eye be?
steps: Same distance on the other side.

learn.reallife: Dancers in Chhau and Kathakali wear masks and face paint with matching halves.

games.title: Mirror facts
items: A mirror swaps left and right.
Your right hand looks like a left hand in the mirror.
A mirror swaps top and bottom.
Up stays up in a standing mirror.
A mirror on the fold line can complete a symmetrical half-picture.
The reflection shows the other half.
A mask with one big eye and one small eye is symmetrical.

quiz.q: You wink your right eye at a mirror. Which eye winks in the mirror image?
quiz.explain: A mirror swaps left and right.
steps: A mirror swaps left and right.
Your right eye winks, so the image's left eye winks.

quiz.q: An arrow points to the right. How does it look in a mirror beside it?
quiz.explain: Left and right swap.
steps: A mirror beside it swaps left and right.
An arrow pointing right looks like it points left.

quiz.q: When is a mask symmetrical?
quiz.explain: Matching halves make it symmetrical.
steps: A shape is symmetrical when its two halves match.
A nose, colour or size does not decide it.
Answer: When its two halves match

quiz.q: A mask has 3 dots on its left cheek. How many on the right cheek for symmetry?
quiz.explain: Same as the left: 3.
steps: For symmetry, the right cheek must match the left.
So the right cheek has 3 dots.

quiz.q: Put a mirror along the middle of half a heart. What do you see?
quiz.explain: The mirror shows the other half.
steps: The mirror shows the other half of the heart.
Half + its reflection = the whole heart.

quiz.q: Which word looks the SAME in a mirror held to the side?
quiz.explain: T and O are symmetrical, and TOOT reads the same backwards.
steps: A side mirror swaps left and right, so the word reads backwards.
TOOT backwards is TOOT, and T and O are symmetrical.
CAKE, BOOK and FUN have letters like C, K, B, F, N that do not match.
quiz.mistake: Picks a word with B or K

quiz.q: In a mirror, does your head appear at the top or the bottom?
quiz.explain: A standing mirror swaps left and right, not top and bottom.
steps: A standing mirror swaps left and right.
It does not swap top and bottom.
So your head stays at the top.

quiz.q: A mask's left half has 2 horns and 1 eye. The right half has 2 horns and 2 eyes. Is it symmetrical?
quiz.explain: The eyes do not match.
steps: Left: 2 horns and 1 eye. Right: 2 horns and 2 eyes.
The horns match, but 1 eye ≠ 2 eyes.
So the halves do not match.

teach.ask: Gappu waves his right wing at the mirror. He thinks the mirror bird uses its right wing too. Is he right?
teach.praise: The mirror swaps left and right, so the mirror bird uses its left wing! Chirp!
teach.nudge: Does a mirror keep left as left?

revise.summary: A mirror image looks the same but with left and right swapped. A mirror on the middle line of a half-picture completes a symmetrical shape.
focus: Know how a mirror swaps left and right.
Check if a mask is symmetrical.
Complete a shape with a mirror.
remember: Raise your right hand: the mirror image raises its left.
An eye 3 cm left of the middle → other eye 3 cm right.
TOOT looks the same in a side mirror.
traps: A mirror does not copy exactly. It swaps left and right.
A standing mirror does not swap top and bottom.
Check every part: eyes, horns and dots must all match.

learn.hook: Colour the right side so it mirrors the left. Move a ball to make both sides match!
points: Odd one out: find the shape that is different and say why.
To colour boxes so one side mirrors the other, copy each coloured box across the middle line, at the same distance.
In a row of 6 boxes, box 1 mirrors box 6, box 2 mirrors box 5, box 3 mirrors box 4.
Balls on two sides: if the left has 5 and the right has 3, move 1 ball across to make 4 and 4.

example.q: Left side has 7 balls and right side has 3. How many should move to make the sides match?

learn.reallife: Puzzle books and games at fairs often use mirror and symmetry challenges.

quiz.q: In a row of 6 boxes, box 2 is coloured. Which box number must be coloured to mirror it?
quiz.explain: Box 2 is 2nd from the left, so its partner is 2nd from the right: box 5.
steps: Box 1 mirrors box 6, box 2 mirrors box 5, box 3 mirrors box 4.
Its partner is 2nd from the right: box 5.

quiz.q: In a row of 8 boxes, box 1 is coloured. Which box number mirrors it?
quiz.explain: 1st from the left ↔ 1st from the right.
steps: In a row of 8 boxes, box 1 is 1st from the left.
Its partner is 1st from the right.

quiz.q: Left has 6 balls, right has 2. How many should move from left to right?
quiz.explain: 8 in all, 4 each. Move 6 − 4 = 2.

quiz.q: Odd one out: square, rectangle, circle, triangle. Which reason is right for the circle?
quiz.explain: The others all have corners.
steps: Square, rectangle and triangle all have corners.

quiz.q: Odd one out: A, H, F, T. Which one is not symmetrical?
quiz.explain: A, H and T match when folded down the middle. F does not.
steps: Fold each letter down the middle.
A, H and T match. F does not.

quiz.q: A 3 by 3 grid has the middle column as the fold line. The top-left box is coloured. Which box mirrors it?
quiz.explain: Same row, other side of the fold.
steps: The fold line is the middle column.
The mirror box is in the same row, on the other side.
quiz.mistake: Picks a box in the same column

quiz.q: Left: 3 red balls, right: 3 red balls. Do the sides match?
quiz.explain: Both sides have the same.
steps: Left has 3 balls. Right has 3 balls.

quiz.q: Left has 10 balls and right has 4. After moving, each side has the same. How many on each side?

teach.ask: Gappu has 8 seeds on his left and 2 on his right. How can he make both sides match?
teach.praise: 10 seeds, 5 each side. Move 3 from left to right! Chirp!
teach.nudge: How many should be on each side?

revise.summary: Symmetry puzzles: find the odd one out with a reason, colour boxes to mirror across the middle, and move balls to make both sides equal.
focus: Find mirror boxes in a row.
Find the odd one out and give a reason.
Make both sides have equal balls.
remember: Left 7, right 3: total 10, 5 each, move 2.
Each side = total ÷ 2.
traps: Don't move the whole difference. Move half of it.
The mirror box is not the next box.
If both sides are already equal, no move is needed.

learn.hook: Can you cover a floor with circles and leave no gaps? Try squares instead!
points: Tiling means covering a space with shapes, with no gaps and no overlaps.
Squares, rectangles, triangles and hexagons can tile a floor. Circles leave gaps.
Choose cut-outs that fill a shape exactly, without gaps.
Make a tile by joining shapes, like two triangles into a square, and repeat it to make a path.
The repeating unit is the smallest part that repeats to make the whole pattern.

example.q: A path repeats: red square, blue triangle, blue triangle. What is the repeating unit?
steps: Look for the part that comes again.
Red square, blue triangle, blue triangle

learn.reallife: Floors of homes, temples and railway stations are tiled with repeating shapes.

games.title: Tiling facts
items: Circles cover a floor with no gaps.
Two equal triangles can make a square tile.
Cut a square corner to corner.
A repeating unit comes again and again.
That is how tiling patterns are made.

quiz.q: Which shape leaves gaps when tiling?
quiz.explain: Circles cannot fit together without gaps.
steps: Tiling leaves no gaps and no overlaps.
Squares, rectangles and hexagons fit together.
Circles cannot fit together without gaps.

quiz.q: What does tiling mean?
options: Covering a space with no gaps or overlaps
quiz.explain: Tiles fit edge to edge.
steps: Tiling means covering a space with shapes.
The shapes fit edge to edge with no gaps and no overlaps.
Answer: Covering a space with no gaps or overlaps

quiz.q: A path goes ⬛🔺⬛🔺⬛🔺. What is the repeating unit?
quiz.explain: Square then triangle repeats.
steps: Look for the part that comes again: ⬛🔺 | ⬛🔺 | ⬛🔺.

quiz.q: How many small square tiles cover a path 5 tiles long and 2 tiles wide?
steps: The path is 5 tiles long and 2 tiles wide.

quiz.q: Two equal triangles cut from a square are joined back. What tile do they make?
quiz.explain: The two halves rebuild the square.
steps: The two triangles were cut from a square.
Joining the halves rebuilds the whole square.

quiz.q: A pattern's unit is red, blue, blue. How many blues in 4 units?
quiz.explain: 2 blues per unit × 4 = 8.
steps: Each unit red, blue, blue has 2 blues.

quiz.q: Which cut-out fills a square hole with no gap?
options: A square of the same size
A triangle of half the size
quiz.explain: Only a same-size square fits exactly.
steps: To fill a square hole with no gap, the piece must match exactly.
A bigger square will not fit. A circle or half-triangle leaves gaps.
Answer: A square of the same size
quiz.mistake: Picks a shape that leaves gaps

quiz.q: Which shape is often seen in honeycomb tiling?
quiz.explain: Bees make 6-sided cells that fit together.
steps: Bees make 6-sided cells that fit together.

teach.ask: Gappu wants to cover his nest floor with leaf tiles. Should he use round or square leaves?
teach.praise: Square leaves fit with no gaps; round ones leave gaps! Chirp!
teach.nudge: Which shape fits together with no gaps?

revise.summary: Tiling means covering a space with shapes, with no gaps and no overlaps. Squares, rectangles, triangles and hexagons tile; circles leave gaps.
focus: Know which shapes tile.
Find the repeating unit of a path.
Count tiles and parts of units.
remember: Circles leave gaps.
Two triangles cut from a square make the square again.
Path 5 long, 2 wide = 10 tiles. Honeycombs use hexagons.
traps: Overlapping is not tiling.
The repeating unit is not just one shape.
Count every piece in the unit when finding totals.

learn.hook: 'The ride is next to the food stall, opposite the balloon man.' Can you find it?
points: We can find a place from a description using words like next to, opposite, behind, in front of, between.
Guessing game: think of a place. Others ask yes/no questions to find it.
Good questions cut the choices in half: 'Is it near the gate?'
Each answer rules out some places, until only one is left.

example.q: 8 stalls. Each good yes/no question halves the choices. How many questions to find one stall?

learn.reallife: When you ask a shopkeeper 'Where is the toy stall?', they describe its place with such words.

games.title: Place words
items: 'Between' means in the middle of two things.
Like the cube between two boxes.
A yes/no question has only two answers.
A good question can rule out many places.

quiz.q: The giant wheel is between the food stall and the toy stall. Where is it?
options: On top of the toy stall
In the middle of the two
quiz.explain: Between means in the middle.
steps: Between means in the middle of two things.
Food stall | giant wheel | toy stall.
Answer: In the middle of the two

quiz.q: Which question is a yes/no question?
quiz.explain: It can only be answered yes or no.
steps: A yes/no question can only be answered yes or no.
How far, what colour and where need other answers.
Answer: Is it near the gate?

quiz.q: There are 8 stalls. After the answer to 'Is it on the left half?', how many choices remain?
quiz.explain: Half of 8 is 4.
steps: A good yes/no question halves the choices.

quiz.q: Sunil's stall is opposite the ice-cream stall. What does that mean?
options: It faces the ice-cream stall across the path
quiz.explain: Opposite means facing across.
steps: Sunil's stall faces the ice-cream stall across the path.
It does not mean next to.
Answer: It faces the ice-cream stall across the path

quiz.q: A clue: 'It is next to the gate and not the shoe stall.' The stalls next to the gate are shoes and bangles. Which is it?
quiz.explain: Next to the gate and not shoes leaves bangles.

quiz.q: 16 places. Each good question halves the choices. How many questions to get to 1?
quiz.explain: 16 → 8 → 4 → 2 → 1: 4 questions.

quiz.q: Which is the BEST first question to find a stall among 10?
options: Is it on the left side of the fair?
quiz.explain: It rules out about half the stalls at once.
steps: A good first question rules out about half the stalls.
'Is it the kite stall?' rules out only one stall.
'Is it on the left side?' cuts the choices in half.
Answer: Is it on the left side of the fair?
quiz.mistake: Guesses one stall at a time

quiz.q: A seat on the giant wheel is the 3rd from the top on the right side. What helps you find it?
options: Counting from the top on the right side
Counting from the bottom on the left
quiz.explain: Follow the description exactly.
steps: The seat is 3rd from the top on the right side.
Follow the description exactly: right side, count from the top.
Answer: Counting from the top on the right side

teach.ask: Gappu thought of a tree in the park. How can his friends find it with few questions?
teach.praise: Ask yes/no questions that split the trees in half each time! Chirp!
teach.nudge: Which question rules out the most trees?

revise.summary: We find places using words like next to, opposite and between. In a guessing game, good yes/no questions cut the choices in half.
focus: Use position words to find places.
Ask good yes/no questions.
Count how many questions are needed.
remember: Between = in the middle. Opposite = facing across.
8 stalls: 8 → 4 → 2 → 1 = 3 questions.
16 places: 4 questions.
traps: Opposite does not mean next to.
Guessing one stall at a time is not a good question.
Count from the place the description says.

learn.hook: Dada and Dadi are lost at the fair! Use the map to find them.
points: A map is a drawing of a place from above. Signs show things: a ferris wheel, food, toilets, the gate.
Direction words: go forward, turn left, turn right, go back.
Follow a route step by step: 'From the gate, go forward to the food stall, turn right, walk to the pottery stall.'
Give directions using landmarks: 'Turn left at the giant wheel.'
Your left and right depend on which way you are facing.

example.q: From the gate, go forward 2 stalls, then turn right and go 1 stall. Map: gate → bangles → food; right of food is pottery.

learn.reallife: Maps help us find our way in a new city, a big station or a mall.

games.title: Follow the route
games.prompt: Gate → forward to food stall → right → toy stall → left → Dada and Dadi
items: Go forward to the food stall
Turn left to find Dada and Dadi

quiz.q: What is a map?
options: A drawing of a place seen from above
quiz.explain: Maps show places as seen from above.
steps: A map is a drawing of a place.
It shows the place as seen from above.
Answer: A drawing of a place seen from above
quiz.mistake: Thinks it is a picture of people

quiz.q: Which direction word tells you to change the way you are facing?
quiz.explain: 'Turn left' or 'turn right' changes your direction. 'Forward' keeps it the same.
steps: 'Turn left' or 'turn right' changes the way you face.

quiz.q: Riya walks forward, then turns left. Which hand side did she turn towards?
quiz.explain: Turning left means towards your left hand.
steps: Turning left means turning towards your left hand.

quiz.q: A route: 'From the gate, go forward to the well, then turn right.' What is the landmark?
quiz.explain: The well is the place where you turn.
steps: A landmark is where something happens on the route.
You turn right at the well.
So the well is the landmark.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a landmark is the start

quiz.q: A map shows: Gate → Kites → Food → Rides in a straight line. Walking forward from the gate, which stall comes second?
quiz.explain: First kites, then food.
steps: Walking forward from the gate: 1st kites, 2nd food.
The gate is the start, not a stall.

quiz.q: Which directions are better?
options: Go forward to the giant wheel and turn left
quiz.explain: Clear directions use landmarks and turn words.
steps: Clear directions use landmarks and turn words.
'Go forward to the giant wheel and turn left' has both.
'Walk a bit' and 'over there' are vague.
Answer: Go forward to the giant wheel and turn left

quiz.q: Raju faces the gate. The food stall is on his right. He turns around. Where is the food stall now?
quiz.explain: Turning around swaps left and right.
steps: The food stall is on Raju's right.
Turning around swaps left and right.
So it is now on his left.
quiz.mistake: Thinks it stays on the right

quiz.q: From home, Sita goes forward 3 blocks, turns right and goes 2 blocks. How many blocks did she walk?

teach.ask: Gappu wants to tell his friend how to reach the pond from the big tree. What should he say?
teach.praise: Go forward to the big rock, turn left, and the pond is right there! Chirp!

revise.summary: A map is a drawing of a place from above. We follow and give directions with words like forward, turn left and turn right, and landmarks.
focus: Read a simple map.
Follow a route step by step.
Give clear directions with landmarks.
remember: Forward keeps direction. Turn changes it.
Turning around swaps your left and right.
Gate → bangles → food, turn right → pottery.
traps: Don't count the gate as a stall.
Don't mix up left and right.
Vague words like 'over there' are not good directions.

learn.hook: The fair is closing! Find the path through the maze to the exit gate.
points: A maze has paths and walls. Only some paths reach the exit.
Trace with your finger. If you hit a dead end, go back to the last turn and try another way.
Starting from the exit and working backwards can also help.
Describe your route: 'Right at the balloon stall, left at the well, straight to the gate.'
Name the landmarks you pass, so others can follow the same path.

example.q: A maze has 3 paths from the start. Path A hits a wall, path B hits a wall. Which path should you try?
steps: A and B are dead ends.

learn.reallife: Garden mazes and puzzle books are fun ways to practise planning a route.

games.title: Describe the route
items: Go straight to the balloon stall
Turn left to the exit gate

games.title: Maze tips
items: At a dead end, go back to the last turn.
Every path in a maze reaches the exit.
Naming landmarks helps others follow your route.
Working backwards from the exit can help.

quiz.q: What should you do at a dead end in a maze?
options: Go back to the last turn and try another way
quiz.explain: Going back lets you try a new path.
steps: At a dead end, the path is blocked.
Go back to the last turn.
Answer: Go back to the last turn and try another way

quiz.q: What is a landmark?
options: Something easy to notice that helps you find the way
quiz.explain: Landmarks like a well or a big tree help describe a route.
steps: A landmark is something easy to notice.
Like a well or a big tree, it helps you find the way.
Answer: Something easy to notice that helps you find the way

quiz.q: A maze has 4 paths from the start. 3 are dead ends. How many reach the exit?
steps: Paths from the start = 4. Dead ends = 3.

quiz.q: Which is a clear route description?
options: Turn right at the balloon stall, then left at the well
quiz.explain: It names turns and landmarks.
steps: A clear route names turns and landmarks.
'Turn right at the balloon stall, then left at the well' does this.
Answer: Turn right at the balloon stall, then left at the well

quiz.q: Mohan passed the swings, the well and the balloon stall. How many landmarks did he pass?
quiz.explain: Swings, well, balloon stall: 3.

quiz.q: Why can starting from the exit help?
options: You can see which paths lead to it
quiz.explain: Tracing back shows the connected path.
steps: Start at the exit and trace backwards.
You can see which paths lead to it.
Answer: You can see which paths lead to it

quiz.q: A route: right, left, left. Reena did right, left, right. How many turns did she get correct?
quiz.explain: First right ✔, then left ✔, then right ✘.
steps: Route: right, left, left. Reena: right, left, right.

quiz.q: To reach the exit, you need 5 turns. You have made 3. How many more?

teach.ask: Gappu got stuck at a dead end in a maze. What should he do?
teach.praise: Go back to the last turn and try another way! Chirp!
teach.nudge: Where should I go back to?

revise.summary: A maze has paths and walls. At a dead end, go back to the last turn and try another way. Describe your route with turns and landmarks.
focus: Solve a maze.
Work backwards from the exit.
Describe a route clearly.
remember: Dead end → go back to the last turn.
A landmark is easy to notice and helps you find the way.
4 paths, 3 dead ends: 1 path works.
traps: Don't give up at a dead end.
The exit does not move.
Check each turn in order when comparing routes.

learn.hook: The fair is full of stalls: pottery, bangles, food and toys! Which stall is the most popular? Let's collect data!
points: Data is information we collect, like how many people visit each stall.
We can collect data by asking questions and making tally marks.
A table shows the data neatly in rows, so it is easy to read.
From a table we can find which is the most, which is the least, and how many there are in all.

example.q: Riya asked 20 friends about their favourite ride: Giant wheel 9, Merry-go-round 6, Toy train 5. Which ride is liked the most?

learn.reallife: Teachers collect data about attendance, and shopkeepers keep data about what they sell.

games.title: Least to most visitors
games.prompt: Visitors: Pottery 12, Bangles 8, Food 15, Toys 10. Order from fewest to most.

items.text: In a tally, one full bundle stands for ___.
Data is shown neatly in a ___.
Giant wheel 9, Toy train 5: the Giant wheel has ___ more.

quiz.q: Visitors at fair stalls: Pottery 12, Bangles 8, Food 15, Toys 10. Which stall had the most visitors?
quiz.explain: 15 is the biggest number in the table, so the Food stall had the most visitors.
steps: So the Food stall had the most visitors.
quiz.mistake: Picks the first stall in the list instead of comparing

quiz.q: Stall visitors: Pottery 12, Bangles 8, Food 15, Toys 10. Which stall had the fewest visitors?
quiz.explain: 8 is the smallest number, so the Bangles stall had the fewest visitors.
steps: So the Bangles stall had the fewest visitors.

quiz.q: The Pottery stall had 12 visitors and the Toys stall had 10. How many more people visited Pottery?
quiz.explain: Find the difference: 12 − 10 = 2.

quiz.q: Stall visitors: Pottery 12, Bangles 8, Food 15, Toys 10. How many visitors in all?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to add one of the stalls

quiz.q: Meena kept a tally of balloons sold. It has 3 bundles of five and 2 single lines. How many balloons were sold?
quiz.explain: 3 bundles of five make 15. 2 more lines make 17.

quiz.q: Why do we put data in a table?
options: To read and compare it easily
quiz.explain: A table keeps the data neat, so we can quickly read it and compare.
steps: A table keeps data neat in rows.
So we can read it and compare it easily.
Answer: To read and compare it easily
quiz.mistake: Thinks a table is only for decoration

quiz.q: Favourite fair food: Chaat 9, Jalebi 7, Kulfi 9. Which sentence is true?
options: Chaat and Kulfi are liked equally
Chaat is liked by 2 fewer than Jalebi
quiz.explain: Chaat and Kulfi both got 9 votes, so they are liked equally. Jalebi got the fewest.
steps: Chaat and Kulfi both have 9, so they are liked equally.
Jalebi has the fewest, so it is not liked the most.
Answer: Chaat and Kulfi are liked equally
quiz.mistake: Does not compare all the numbers carefully

quiz.q: Favourite rides: Giant wheel 14, Toy train 9. How many more children chose the Giant wheel?
quiz.explain: 14 − 9 = 5. Count on from 9: 10, 11, 12, 13, 14 is 5 steps.

teach.ask: Gappu wants to find out which fruit his bird friends like best. How can he collect and show the data?
teach.praise: Ask, tally, make a table, and see the biggest number! Mango wins!
teach.nudge: How do I find out what everyone likes, and how do I write it down?

revise.summary: Data is information we collect, like visitors at each stall. A table shows data neatly so we can find the most, the least and the total.
focus: Read data from a table.
Find the most and the least.
Find the difference and the total.
remember: Most = biggest number. Least = smallest number.
Giant wheel 9, merry-go-round 6, toy train 5: total 20.
Equal numbers mean liked equally.
traps: Don't pick the first row. Compare all numbers.
Don't mix up fewest and most.
Don't add when asked how many more.

learn.hook: What if one picture could stand for 5 kites? Pictographs show data with pictures!
points: A pictograph shows data using pictures or symbols.
A key tells what one picture stands for, like 🎈 = 2 balloons.
To read a row, count the pictures and use the key: 4 pictures with 🎈 = 2 means 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 8.
Always read the key first!

example.q: Key: 🪁 = 5 kites. Arjun's row has 🪁🪁🪁. How many kites did he sell?

learn.reallife: Posters and newspapers often use pictographs so people can understand numbers quickly.

games.title: Pictograph facts
items: A key tells what one picture stands for.
The key is the most important part of a pictograph.
In a pictograph, every picture always means 1.
The key can say one picture means 2, 5, 10 or more.
With the same key, a row with more pictures shows more.
Each picture is worth the same, so more pictures means more.

quiz.q: Key: 🍦 = 2 ice creams. Row: 🍦🍦🍦🍦. How many ice creams?
quiz.explain: Each 🍦 means 2. Four pictures: 2, 4, 6, 8.
quiz.mistake: Counts the pictures and forgets the key

quiz.q: Key: 🎈 = 5 balloons. Row: 🎈🎈🎈. How many balloons?
quiz.explain: Each 🎈 means 5. Three pictures: 5, 10, 15.
quiz.mistake: Adds 3 and 5 instead of counting three 5s

quiz.q: What does the key in a pictograph tell us?
quiz.explain: The key tells how many things one picture stands for.
steps: The key tells what one picture stands for.
Answer: What one picture stands for
quiz.mistake: Skips the key when reading a pictograph

quiz.q: Key: 🧸 = 10 toys. The toy stall's row is 🧸🧸🧸🧸. How many toys were sold?
quiz.explain: Each 🧸 means 10. Four pictures: 10, 20, 30, 40.
quiz.mistake: Counts the pictures and forgets the key

quiz.q: Key: 🪁 = 2 kites. Riya sold 12 kites. How many 🪁 pictures are in her row?
quiz.explain: Each picture is 2 kites. Count by 2s to 12: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12. That is 6 pictures.
quiz.mistake: Draws one picture for every kite

quiz.q: Key: ⭐ = 5. Kabir has ⭐⭐⭐ and Aisha has ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐. How many more does Aisha have?
quiz.explain: Kabir has 15 and Aisha has 25. 25 − 15 = 10. Or: 2 more stars × 5 = 10.
quiz.mistake: Counts the extra stars (2) and forgets the key

quiz.q: Key: 🍎 = 3 apples. Row: 🍎🍎🍎🍎🍎. How many apples?
quiz.explain: Each 🍎 means 3. Five pictures: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15.
quiz.mistake: Adds 5 and 3 instead of counting five 3s

quiz.q: Key: 🧁 = 4 cupcakes. Monday: 🧁🧁. Tuesday: 🧁🧁🧁. How many cupcakes in all?
quiz.explain: There are 5 pictures in all, and each is 4 cupcakes. 5 × 4 = 20.
quiz.mistake: Counts only one day or forgets the key

teach.ask: Gappu sees a pictograph with 3 🐛 pictures and a key that says 🐛 = 5. He thinks there are 3 worms. Is he right?
teach.praise: Each picture means 5, so 3 pictures are 15 worms! I'll always read the key.
teach.nudge: What does the key say one picture means?

revise.summary: A pictograph shows data with pictures. The key tells what one picture stands for. Always read the key first.
focus: Read a pictograph using the key.
Find totals from pictures.
Draw a pictograph with a key.
remember: 4 pictures with 🎈 = 2 → 8.
🪁 = 5: three pictures → 15 kites.
Number = pictures × key value.
traps: Don't count the pictures and forget the key.
Don't add the key and the count.
Don't draw one picture for every thing when the key is bigger.

learn.hook: 18 laddoos and 3 hungry friends at the fair. How many does each one get? Division will tell us!
points: Division means sharing equally or making equal groups.
Sharing: 12 bangles shared by 3 girls gives 4 each. We write 12 ÷ 3 = 4.
Grouping: 12 bangles put in bags of 4 fill 3 bags. 12 ÷ 4 = 3.
Division is the opposite of multiplication: 3 × 4 = 12, so 12 ÷ 3 = 4.
We can also take away the same number again and again: 12 − 4 − 4 − 4 = 0. We took away 4 three times.

example.q: At the fair, 20 clay pots are packed with 5 pots in each box. How many boxes are needed?

learn.reallife: Packing sweets into boxes or dividing players into teams for kho-kho uses division.

quiz.q: 18 laddoos are shared equally by 3 children. How many laddoos does each child get?
What is 20 ÷ 4?
24 bangles are packed with 4 bangles in each box. How many boxes are needed?
quiz.explain: Make groups of 4: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24. That is 6 groups. 24 ÷ 4 = 6.

quiz.q: Which multiplication fact helps to find 15 ÷ 3?
quiz.explain: 3 × 5 = 15 tells us that 15 shared into 3 groups gives 5 each. So 15 ÷ 3 = 5.
steps: Division is the opposite of multiplication.
We need a fact that makes 15 using 3.
quiz.mistake: Does not see division as the opposite of multiplication

quiz.q: Kabir has 14 balloons. He ties them in bunches of 2. How many bunches does he make?
quiz.explain: Count by 2s to 14: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14. That is 7 bunches.

quiz.q: 30 people want to ride the toy train. Each coach holds 10 people. How many coaches will be filled?
quiz.explain: Make groups of 10: 10, 20, 30. That is 3 coaches. 30 ÷ 10 = 3.

quiz.q: Aisha takes away 5 again and again from 25 until nothing is left. How many times does she take away 5?
16 kulfis are shared equally among 4 friends. How many kulfis does each friend get?
quiz.mistake: Takes away 4 from 16 instead of sharing

teach.ask: Gappu has 12 seeds and wants to give them equally to his 4 baby cousins. How can he work out how many each gets?
teach.praise: 12 ÷ 4 = 3! Each cousin gets 3 seeds. Sharing is caring!
teach.nudge: How can I make sure every cousin gets the same number?

revise.summary: Division means sharing equally or making equal groups. It is the opposite of multiplication.
focus: Divide by sharing.
Divide by grouping.
Use a times fact to divide.
remember: 12 shared by 3 = 4. 12 in bags of 4 = 3 bags.
20 pots in boxes of 5 = 4 boxes.
traps: Don't take away once. Share equally.
Don't stop one step too early.
Division and multiplication are linked.
